READ CONTRACT shared by NXS-LOCAL-0159 and NXS-LOCAL-0160 (both build to it; neither changes it without a RELAY_QUESTION). GET /devices/{id}/inventory -> 200 {device_id, collected_at (ISO-8601, nullable when no run), job: JobView|null, contexts: [{context: string (\"physical\" or the VSID / vsys id), interfaces: [{name, parent (nullable), kind (physical|vlan|subinterface|loopback|bond|tunnel|other), state (up|down|unknown), addresses: [{address (with prefix), family (ipv4|ipv6), role (member|cluster_virtual)}]}], routes: [{destination, next_hop (nullable), interface (nullable), protocol (static|connected|default|ospf|bgp|rip|host|kernel|unknown), table (nullable)}]}]}. 404 {error: NOT_FOUND}. GET /clusters/{cluster_member_ref}/inventory -> 200 {cluster_member_ref, members: [{device_id, hostname (nullable)}], contexts: [{context, interfaces: [{name, kind, addresses: [...same as above...], presence: \"all\" | [device_id...], differences: [{device_id, field, value}]}], routes: [{destination, next_hop, interface, protocol, presence, differences}]}]}. Keys exactly as spelled, snake_case. The persistence model behind it (migration V13, additive): device_inventory_run(run_id PK, device_id FK devices, job_id, collected_at, context_count), device_interface(interface_id PK, run_id FK, context, name, parent, kind, state), device_interface_address(address_id PK, interface_id FK, address, family, role), device_route(route_id PK, run_id FK, context, destination, next_hop, interface, protocol, route_table). DeviceInventoryRepository (persistence module): recordRun(InventoryRun) writes one run with all children in one transaction; findLatestRun(deviceId) -> Optional<InventoryRun>; findLatestRuns(List<String> deviceIds). InventoryRun / InventoryContext / InventoryInterface / InventoryAddress / InventoryRoute are Java records in persistence.device.inventory with exactly the fields above.

baseline.what_exists: Merged: devices/endpoints with V12 columns (observed_hostname/model/software_version/ha_role, cluster_member_ref, virtual_system_ref, enrollment_state, disabled); worker.confirm (ConfirmJobExecutor as a C2-compliant executor sibling of StepExecutor, WorkerClaimLoop claiming one job at a time, CheckPoint/PaloAlto confirm parsers, Vendor enum); worker.transport (SshExecTransport, PanXmlApiTransport, CompositeDeviceTransport routing by transport kind, WorkerBootstrap); job-engine: JobAdmissionService.submit(capabilityId, targetDeviceId, idempotencyKey, actor, actionId) with ConfirmCapabilityIds as the only DRAFT exception, DeviceEnrollmentReadPort, StepExecutor, StepParser(String)->ParsedStepResult, EvidenceWriterPort, JobLeaseRepository; persistence: JooqDeviceRepository, TransactionBoundary/TransactionBoundaryFactory, JobRecordDao; capability-registry: YAML specs (cp_gaia_inventory.yaml is a two-command placeholder from B1-5, superseded in scope by 13F section 7 -- replace it). Python know-how (read, never import, never port): the shapes the earlier collectors parsed. Check Point interfaces: 'ip -details -4 addr show' -- header lines start with an index digit and contain ':', name is the second colon field, '@' splits name from parent, 'inet ' lines carry CIDR in the second token; lo is a loopback; UP must be read from the flag list inside '<...>' not by substring. Routes: 'ip -4 route show table all' -- 'default' means 0.0.0.0/0, 'blackhole' rows carry the destination second, tokens 'via' next hop, 'dev' interface, 'proto' protocol, 'table' table; local/broadcast rows and 127.x rows are not routes. Cluster VIPs: 'cphaprob -a -m if' -- only the block after a line beginning 'virtual cluster interfaces:' (case-insensitive) up to the next section; first token interface name, first IPv4 literal the address; everything from this read is role cluster_virtual, everything from ip addr is role member. HA: 'cphaprob stat' -- the local row carries '(local)'; state token from the fixed vocabulary; the 'mode' line gives the cluster mode (Virtual System Load Sharing, Load Sharing multicast/unicast, High Availability / new mode, VRRP). VSX: 'vsx stat -v' -- rows begin with the VSID then '|'; the VSID column is the only trustworthy one. Palo Alto: interfaces under result/ifnet/entry with leaves name, ip, vsys, zone, fwd (fwd text contains 'vr:<name>'); a firewall may return several address elements per entry and a separate IPv6 element -- read all of them; entries without an address are still interfaces (HA links). Routes under the result's route container entries with leaves destination, nexthop ('0.0.0.0' means none), interface (strip an '@vsysN' suffix), virtual-router, flags (letters: S static, C connected, O OSPF, B BGP, R RIP, H host, A active, E ECMP). Fixture files under tests/fixtures/{cp,vsx,panorama} show these shapes with documentation addresses; write your own Java fixtures in the same spirit, do not read the Python parsers' code as a design.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Every public type names the clause it implements (14C D-n, 13F section n, C2/C4 section n).
Do NOT use './ui2/gradlew -p ui2 build' without '-x :integration-tests:test'. Do not run the full Python pytest suite. Eleven Gradle subprojects.

If a contract clause and this packet disagree, raise a RELAY_QUESTION and STOP; never reconcile silently and never relax a direction test.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the PR or code comments.
Commit early and often. Open the PR at the end; do not merge. The PR body carries a summary and a test plan only.

in: FIRST COMMIT, before anything else: the persistence types and repository interface the shared read contract names (persistence.device.inventory: InventoryRun, InventoryContext, InventoryInterface, InventoryAddress, InventoryRoute records; DeviceInventoryRepository interface with recordRun, findLatestRun, findLatestRuns) plus migration V13 (additive tables exactly as the contract lists, with indexes on device_id+collected_at and run_id) and JooqDeviceInventoryRepository. Push that commit to the lane immediately so NXS-LOCAL-0160 can build on it.

Job kind and admission: InventoryCapabilityIds (cp_inventory_collect, pan_inventory_collect); JobAdmissionService admits them only when the device is ENROLLED and not disabled (existing F4 refusal for DRAFT stays; confirm stays the only exception); a test proves inventory against DRAFT is DEVICE_NOT_ELIGIBLE and against ENROLLED is Admitted. Capability YAML specs for the two, CAP_OFFLINE, FIXTURE_ONLY, revalidation_plan_ref pointing at 14C section 5; delete cp_gaia_inventory.yaml and update any test that named it.

Parsers (worker.inventory.cp and worker.inventory.pan), each a pure function from output text to the persistence records, each with fixtures and tests: CheckPointIpAddrParser (IPv4 and IPv6 forms), CheckPointIpRouteParser, CheckPointClusterVirtualInterfaceParser, CheckPointHaStateParser (role + cluster mode, local row only), CheckPointVsxStatParser (VSIDs only); PaloAltoInterfaceParser (all address elements, IPv6, address-less interfaces kept, vsys and virtual router kept), PaloAltoRouteParser (protocol from flags, virtual-router as table, container-anchored). Unknown tokens map to 'unknown', never to a guess; a malformed line is skipped and counted, never fatal.

Read plan: InventoryReadPlan per vendor as data (14C section 3 exact strings; VSX per-context composite lines; Palo Alto per-vsys parameter), with a test asserting the plan equals the section 3 set literally (the closed-set pattern DeviceFirstContactCommandSet uses). Check Point reads run in one interactive session per device, paced; the plan expresses that as ordered exec steps on one TransportSession.

InventoryJobExecutor (worker.inventory): claims inventory_collect jobs through the existing lease/fencing/heartbeat path exactly as ConfirmJobExecutor does (copy its C2 discipline, share code where a small extraction is clean), resolves the credential from the store, runs the plan through DeviceTransport, parses, assembles one InventoryRun with contexts (physical plus each VSID/vsys), and calls recordRun inside one transaction; failure leaves no partial run; identity mismatch on this contact follows 13F ID-M1..M4 (warn, audit, continue; strict posture refuses). Register the executor in WorkerClaimLoop next to the confirm so one worker process serves both kinds.

Tests: parser fixture tests; the closed-set plan test; admission test; an end-to-end executor test against a scripted fake DeviceTransport for a Check Point cluster member with two VSIDs and for a Palo Alto firewall with two vsys, asserting the recorded run's contexts, addresses (roles) and routes; a worker-dies test (lease lapses, no run recorded); repository test at the persistence unit level with the existing fakes. Architecture tests untouched and green.
out: Any live device contact, any gate row, any change to CAP_OFFLINE; the configuration_collect kind (next movement); the HTTP read surface and the screens (0160); scheduler; changes to the confirm, peer follow or identity policy beyond reusing them; renaming Java packages.

unresolved_risks: Every parser is UNVERIFIED against a real device/firewall (14C section 3's own status): Check Point channel differs from the earlier product's proven payload; Palo Alto show interface all / show routing route shapes are unproven. Corrections belong in these classes alone once 14C section 5's measurement lands.

Palo Alto vsys context assignment for routes falls back to an interface-name lookup or a default vsys when a route's own interface field carries no @vsysN suffix -- a documented best-effort reading of an unmeasured shape (PaloAltoRouteParser javadoc), not a fabricated certainty.

Identity mismatch on an already-ENROLLED device has no persisted warning write path today (only the confirm's own recordConfirmSuccess ever writes an identity baseline) -- 'warn and continue' currently means the run proceeds; a visible, persisted warning marker on inventory-collect contact is a successor movement's write path, not invented here.

The HA-role reads inventory issues (cphaprob stat, both physical and per-VSID) are parsed but never persisted -- V13 names no HA-role column; they exist only to keep the paced session's command sequence exactly as 14C section 3 lists it.
